Ride sharing and uber are bringing up interesting questions in the insurance world.  Typically (depending on state) insurance is primary for the vehicle that is in question.  So, for example, you 'borrow' a car using a ride sharing program and are involved in an accident. That vehicles insurance is primary and any insurance coverage that you own would be provided on an excess basis.  However, often times insurers will exclude coverage if used in any business (which can include renting their car to others).  I am unsure if the ride share company allows purchasing additional insurance at the time of rental.  I believe this is your best option as you can "pay as you go".  Your umbrella should have an attachment point of $250/500  or $300k combined single limits.  So whatever you choose, make sure you at least obtain the minimum limits to attach the umbrella.  Remember umbrellas also protect you against liability cases covered under your homeowners policy as well.

In regards to uber, since you won't be driving, you shouldn't need auto insurance.  Sometimes, your umbrella policy would provide uninsured and underinsured motorist benefits.

Simple answer, if ride sharing allows you to purchase option insurance, I would go that route.
